attributes.residual: MIXED. (a) STACK_LAYOUT, and this is the most valuable open lead: the 'missing local' at 108(r1) is NOT missing - it is `result`, which the target keeps in MEMORY (stw 0 at 0x40 on entry, stw at 0x5f8 for `result = 1`, lwz r3 at 0x658 to return it) while ours keeps it in a register (mr at @644). That is a spill decision, and it is downstream of the real defect: target's frame is 200 bytes with locals at 8..120 (bufC@12, bufB@44, bufA@76, result@108, f64 scratch@112) whereas ours is 256 with locals at 8..176 and 60 bytes of reserved-but-unused slots below the buffers at 8..68. Under the (load-bearing) opt_lifetimes-off pragma the frame tracks the DECLARED local count, so our reconstruction declares roughly 14 more locals than the original. Reducing/scoping the 22 declared scalars (note `boff` is dead in 3 of its 4 loops) is the next axis and should be run as a declaration-reconstruction pass, not an alias pass. (b) REGISTER_ONLY: the remaining target-only +4 add are the same base+index rematerialization documented in the companion law.
